description: Evidence classification taxonomy for AI transformation readiness audit. Defines what constitutes valid evidence for each score level.

0.label: Absent
0.description: No evidence found in the document. Document is silent on this topic.
0.antipattern_interpretation: Anti-pattern not detected. Clean area only when meaningfully tested.
0.evidence_requirements: None required. Silence is valid data but may indicate unknown coverage.

1.label: Aspirational
1.description: Vague intent, buzzwords, or planned initiatives only. No evidence of operational practice.
1.maturity_interpretation: Intent without implementation. Plans = Score 1 max.
1.antipattern_interpretation: Minor indicators or emerging risk signals.
evidence_examples: We plan to define an AI governance model
Teams are interested in generative AI

2.label: Operational
2.description: Behavior or process is described and functioning. Evidence of actual practice, not just policy.
2.maturity_interpretation: Capability exists and is practiced. Not yet embedded.
2.antipattern_interpretation: Pattern is present and causing friction.
evidence_examples: The AI review forum meets monthly with product, security, and data owners
Pilot learnings are recorded and reused
Data owners publish definitions and access rules
AI quality is evaluated before release

3.label: Embedded
3.description: Explicit mechanisms, enforcement, automation, measurement, or cultural norms. Evidence of mature systematic practice.
3.maturity_interpretation: Mature capability with enforcement, measurement, and learning loops.
3.antipattern_interpretation: Pattern is deeply embedded and structural.
evidence_examples: Production AI releases can be traced to model, prompt, data, and evaluation versions
Guardrails and escalation paths are tested before deployment
Service areas own AI value metrics after launch
Portfolio decisions kill, continue, or scale AI initiatives based on evidence

evidence_quality_rules: Direct quotes from the document are the strongest evidence
References to tools, processes, metrics, owners, decisions, or artifacts are evidence only when usage is described
Future tense caps maturity score at 1
Policy without operating proof scores lower than measured practice
Specific learning loops, release controls, evaluation results, and ownership records strengthen evidence quality
Generic AI jargon without context is weak evidence

evidence_categories.description: Orthogonal to score. Every evidence_quote captured in Phase 1 must be tagged with exactly one category.

categories.Policy: Written rules, standards, or formal documents that declare intent.
categories.Process: Recurring human practices or workflows that are described as actually happening.
categories.Operational: Day-to-day AI delivery, review, support, service ownership activities, AI usage reports, or AI spend dashboards.
categories.Automation: Code, platform features, pipelines, tests, monitoring, model routing, caching, quota enforcement, budget alerts, or controls that enforce without manual effort.
categories.Accountability: Mechanisms that assign ownership, decision rights, obligations, consequences, AI owners, application owners, or cost owners.
categories.Architecture: Service, platform, integration, data, or business architecture evidence.
categories.Data: Data ownership, quality, lineage, semantic context, retrieval, privacy, or access evidence.
categories.Governance: Risk, approval, auditability, responsible AI, security, legal, compliance, budget guardrail, model approval, or usage-policy evidence.
categories.Learning: Pilot feedback, retrospectives, communities, playbooks, reuse, or competence flow evidence.
categories.Value: Impact statements, baselines, outcome measures, unit economics, cost per business outcome, ROI/TVO, portfolio logic, or value realization evidence.

tagging_rules: Every evidence_quote MUST carry exactly one allowed category.
If a quote could fit multiple categories, pick the dominant one.
Automation supersedes Policy when the quote describes enforcement.
Learning supersedes Process when the quote describes reusable lessons or competence flow.

false_positive_guards: Mentioning an AI tool does not prove AI readiness
A pilot does not prove scalable capability
A policy does not prove governance is embedded
A model registry does not prove release control
A data catalog does not prove business meaning or retrieval quality
Guardrail claims require testing or operating evidence
AI spend dashboards alone do not prove AI readiness
AI cost visibility is readiness evidence only when connected to value, ownership, routing, guardrails, and measurable outcomes
